learning_objective: The learner will examine a curriculum map and find all six gaps and mismatches in it, with no more than one incorrect mark.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** curriculum-map-gap-finder
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** examine
**Learning Objective:** The learner will examine a curriculum map and find all six gaps and mismatches in it, with no more than one incorrect mark. **Prerequisites:** Curriculum Map, Outcome Coverage, Assessment Alignment, Content Gap, Bloom Cognitive Levels (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner marks the problems they find on the map and presses Check. The learner passes when all six problems in the Content table are marked and at most one other mark is wrong. Only the first Check counts as evidence. Opening the problem types is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) An outcome with a matching topic is covered. (2) Content with no outcome is always harmless. (3) A quiz item at any level checks any outcome on its topic. **Instructional Rationale:** Finding gaps in a map is an Analyze-level action, because the learner must examine each connection and decide which is missing, extra, or at the wrong level. A map with several kinds of problem teaches the learner to look in every direction. **Content:** The four outcomes, with the Bloom level of each verb: - O1: Describe what a watershed is. (Remember) - O2: Explain how water moves through a watershed. (Understand) - O3: Predict how paving changes runoff. (Analyze) - O4: Compare two ways to reduce flooding. (Analyze) The five activities and what each supports: - A1: Reading, "What is a watershed?" supports O1. - A2: Reading, "How water moves" supports O2. - A3: Label a watershed diagram supports O1. - A4: Video of famous rivers supports no outcome. - A5: Group discussion on ways to reduce flooding supports O4. The five quiz items and what each checks: - Q1: Choose the definition of a watershed checks O1. - Q2: Name the parts of a watershed checks O1. - Q3: Choose the word for water flowing over land checks O2, and asks only for recall. - Q4: Choose the term for water soaking into the ground checks O2, and asks only for recall. - Q5: Choose the longest river in the region checks no outcome. The six problems to find: | # | Problem | Type | Why it is a problem | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | O3 has no activity. | Not taught | No activity gives practice at predicting. | | 2 | O3 has no quiz item. | Not checked | Nothing checks whether learners can predict. | | 3 | O4 has no quiz item. | Not checked | The discussion is never checked. | | 4 | A4 supports no outcome. | Content with no outcome | The video adds length and supports no promise. | | 5 | Q5 checks no outcome. | Item with no outcome | The question tests something the resource never promised. | | 6 | O2 is checked only at the recall level. | Level mismatch | O2 asks learners to explain, and both items ask only for recall. | **Provenance:** The outcomes, activities, and quiz items are made up for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative example". The problem types follow the chapter sections "Outcome Coverage", "Assessment Alignment", and "Content Gap". **Rules:** The map has exactly six problems, one per row of the table. A mark is correct when it identifies one of the six, by the outcome, activity, or item and the problem type. The learner may mark an outcome as unchecked or untaught, an activity or item as having no outcome, and an outcome as checked at the wrong level. **Learner Activity:** 1. The sim shows the map as a grid of outcomes against activities and quiz items, with the Bloom level of each outcome. 2. The learner clicks a cell, an activity, an item, or an outcome and chooses the problem type from a short list. 3. The learner may remove a mark. 4. The learner presses Check. 5. The sim shows which of the six were found, which marks were wrong, and the Why text for each missed problem. **Feedback:** One Check counts as evidence, and the learner may try again afterward. Pass: "You found all six problems with [n] wrong marks." Not yet: "You found [n] of 6. Missing: [problems with their Why text]." Wrong marks are named with the reason they are not problems. At a pass it adds "You can find the gaps in a map." **Starting State:** The map with no marks and the prompt "Find six problems in this map." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's Watershed Basics table has three outcomes with outcome 3 neither taught nor checked, and the chapter says outcome coverage is the number of taught and assessed outcomes divided by the number of outcomes. This sim's map is a larger unit with four outcomes.
